name: Hall of Femme DE
_comment_group: One more show under the Snapchat heading. The heading names the
network these frames are cut FOR and the channel is the show they are
cut from, so another show cutting for the same network is one more
folder under it rather than a heading of its own.
Like every channel under this heading it is a frame fetcher rather
than a thumbnail maker: a video goes in and a numbered grid of
vertical stills comes out, each captioned with what was being said
over it.
It is cut to Hall of Femme's design, and that pack is the one to read
first: the frame fetch, the vertical output, the transcription, the
rewrite, the card at the foot of the frame and every number in it are
the same and are named here rather than restated. What makes this show
itself is one sentence long - it is set in Raleway, on a gold card, in
two colours the user pairs per frame - and everything below is that
sentence.
The DE in the name is the account's, the way the FR in Soccer Stories
FR is: it says which of the brand's feeds this is and not what
language the app is in. What lands on the frames is whatever the
video's own voice track was saying, put through the transcription and
the rewrite exactly as on every channel here; nothing in this pack
changes that, and everything the app itself says is English like the
rest of it (see CLAUDE.md).
One thing this pack checked that most of its siblings had no reason
to, and that fitness-story-de - the other DE feed here - checked
before it. Both Raleway files carry 936 codepoints and cover the
umlauts, both cases of the eszett and the low quotes German sets
speech in, so a caption is drawn from the file rather than from
whatever the browser substitutes for a missing glyph - which would be
a different face, at a width nothing measured. Worth stating because a
face chosen for how it looks in English is not automatically a face
that can SET another language, and the check is two minutes against a
cmap.
A separate folder rather than a second colourway of Hall of Femme, for
the reason oh-my-goal-news is a folder of its own: the person picking a
channel at the top of the app picks this or that one and never both,
and these two do not merely disagree about colour - they are set in
different type, which is as far as two packs under one heading go.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not.
_comment_title: What separates this show from the others under the heading: it is set
in Raleway Regular, on a gold card, in colours the user picks per
frame, with a picked word in Raleway Bold.
Everything else - the size, where the lines break, the capitals, the
shape of the card, where it stands on the frame, what a picked word
does - is the Snapchat caption design and is stated once, in
content/presets/snapchat-caption.json. This pack states only what
makes it this show, which is the whole of what a pack under this
Raleway is a text face rather than a display one, and that is a thing a
caption can be set in here only because of the card. Its strokes are
modulated and its terminals fine, and fine terminals are exactly what a
photograph eats: over grain and detail a 400-weight text sans reads as
a grey smear before it reads as words. On a solid ground somebody chose
it stays a text face - which is the same argument Hall of Femme makes
for its hairline and Hoodsiderz for its hand, from a third place on the

_comment_color: The dark green, and it is the channel's own answer - therefore what
every frame is set in until somebody presses a swatch, since a
frame stores no colour of its own until it is given one (see
state.textColorFor). It is one of the two in `colors` below, so the
green swatch is the one that shows as chosen on an untouched frame;
the swatch is found by matching this value rather than by being
listed first, which is why the green sits second in a row that
Green letters on the gold card is the pairing this show opens on.
Both colours are the brand, so which of them is the CARD is a real
decision rather than a default: the card is a fifth of the frame and
reads before anything on it, and the gold is the half of the pair
that carries at that size and at that distance. The green is then
what has to stay legible against it, which at these two values it
comfortably is - they are far enough apart in lightness that the type
holds at caption size on a phone.
The other three pairings are a button away, the inverse among them.
_comment_colors: The two colours this show is set in, offered for the letters and for
the card behind them - two buttons each in the title panel (see
editor.renderColorButtons).
The same two in both lists and in one order, which is what every
pack under this heading does and for their reason: the point is the
PAIRING. Four combinations of a gold and a dark green, and the two
worth having are the two that read. A palette that could only ever
be used one way round would be a palette of one card, and this
show's look is the pairing rather than either colour on its own.
Two colours rather than the three or four its neighbours offer, and
that is the brand and not an unfinished list. Nothing counts these
entries - the panel draws a swatch per colour and the row wraps - so
a third is one string in this file the day the show has one.
Nothing stops the user setting green on green. That is not an
oversight either: the two lists are independent because the pairing
is the feature, and with a palette this short a rule barring the two
matching combinations would be a rule removing half the buttons. The
user can see the caption has gone and presses the other swatch.
`text` reaches the highlight as well as the block - see the note on
`colors` in js/channels.js. This channel's highlight is a different
CUT of the face and not a different colour, so what colour the type
is has one answer and not two. That matters more on a palette of two
than on one of four: with the block green, a highlight left to pick
its own colour from the same list could only ever be gold, and gold
on gold is a picked word that vanishes into its card.
_comment_highlight: A picked word is set in Raleway Bold, in the same colour as the rest
of the block. The highlight here is WEIGHT, which is Hall of Femme's
answer rather than Hoodsiderz's: one family, two cuts, the change of
voice being a change of volume and nothing else.
It is a narrower gap than the pack this is cut from has. Hall of
Femme picks words out at 200 against 800, the two ends of Telegraf,
which on a card is as loud as a box would be. 400 against 700 is the
ordinary text pairing instead, and it is the right one for this
face: Raleway's own extremes are drawn for display, and its Regular
against its Bold is the contrast the family was actually fitted for
- a picked word that is unmistakably heavier at 40px while the line
it sits in stays one sentence in one voice.
Two measurements say it survives the setting, taken the way
Hoodsiderz takes its own. At the preset's 40px the two cuts put
their capitals at the same height to the pixel, so a picked word
neither rides above the line it is part of nor sits inside it. And
twelve capitals come out 293px wide in the Regular against 297 in
the Bold - one percent - so which words are picked out does not
move where the lines break, which is worth knowing on a channel
whose text arrives already wrapped (see js/caption.js). That is the
quiet advantage of staying inside one family: the weight changes
and the fit does not.
The two cuts are two faces here, with two family names, and that is
not a formality: see raleway-regular.json for why a bare 'Raleway'
would let either of them answer and would also collide with the
family the interface itself is set in.
The colour it names is the block's, so the recolour draws exactly
what its neighbours are drawn in and the weight is the whole of the
difference. Stated all the same, for the fallback reason `color`
above is stated - a highlight that changed colour as well as weight
would be two highlights.
The mode and the scope come from the preset, which is where the
argument for picking out words rather than lines lives.
_comment_panel: Gold, and the fill is the one thing about the card this pack
decides: its shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow are the
Snapchat caption design and come from the preset.
It is the first entry in `colors.panel` above as well, so the swatch
that shows as chosen on an untouched frame is the one at the start
of the row. Nothing requires that - the swatch is found by matching
this value rather than by being listed first - and the type's own
colour is deliberately NOT first in its row, which is the same
freedom used the other way round.
The preset's shadow earns its keep under this card more than under
most: a mid-bright gold thrown onto a sunlit still has less to
separate it from the picture than a hot pink or a near-black does,
and the shadow is what keeps the card a graphic lying on the frame.

_comment_branding: No dark gradient. It exists to hold a title legible against the
photograph, and this title is not against the photograph at all - it is
on a card of its own. A scrim over every still would darken forty
pictures to solve a problem the card has already solved.
